title: Axon presentation to Council members: scheduling, attendance and materials, Aug 1 – Oct 5, 2026 (follow-up to W013585)
summary:
The W013585-100626 production includes Lt. Riccardi's 2026-08-19 email "Axon briefing for council" to the Chief, the City Manager, Laurie Strange and Martin McTaggart, stating that Axon wanted to give an in-person executive presentation on its technology and ALPRs, attaching "a sample of how we can structure the day with up to two council members at a time," and asking for help with dates. The production has no reply, no scheduling record and not the attachment. This request asks the City, for 2026-08-01 through 2026-10-05 and for the mailboxes, calendars and text messages of the Chief of Police, the City Manager, Strange, McTaggart, Lt. Riccardi and each Council member (including personal accounts or devices used for City business, City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608), for four things:

- Item 1: communications, with attachments, about the scheduling, format, attendance, agenda or materials of an Axon presentation, briefing or meeting for Council members, including with any axon.com address (search may be limited to "Axon"),
- Item 2: calendar entries for any meeting, call or presentation with Axon personnel, with date, time, location, subject and attendees,
- Item 3: any agenda, sign-in sheet, visitor record, slide deck, handout or other material presented to or left with a Council member, the City Manager or the Chief by Axon at such a session, including material sent before or after,
- Item 4: communications between Police command staff or the City Manager's office and any Council member about the Axon Outpost proposal (File 26-11633) before its 2026-10-05 hearing (search may be limited to "Axon" or "Outpost").

Asks for segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525(b)) and native format, and that a no-records answer be given item by item.

policy_promises.quote: agency must notify requester within 10 calendar days whether it will produce records
policy_promises.tests: Does the City issue a determination by 2026-11-10, and does a multi-mailbox search draw the same § 7922.535(b) extension W013585 did?

policy_promises.policy: Gov. Code § 7920.530 / City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608
policy_promises.quote: a city employee's communications about public business are not excluded from CPRA simply because they have been sent, received, or stored in a personal account
policy_promises.tests: Does the City search Council members' personal accounts and devices for the scheduling and attendance records, or limit the search to City mailboxes?

policy_promises.quote: Any reasonably segregable portion of a record shall be available for inspection
policy_promises.tests: If the City withholds presentation materials or pre-hearing communications, does it produce the segregable parts and identify the exemption per record?

prior_pra_refs.note: Closed 2026-10-30 with 30 files. The 2026-08-19 "Axon briefing for council" email is in that production; no reply, scheduling record or attachment was produced. W013585 searched for "Q-865809" and "Outpost"; the 8/19 email uses neither term in its body, so this request searches on "Axon" and names the City Manager and Council mailboxes.

Filed the same morning. Its item 1(d) asks for the "San Mateo PD Axon council session.pdf" attachment as transmitted; this request's item 3 asks for whatever was actually presented to or left with Council members.
Companion Axon quote request (Q-865809 revisions). The Outpost item approved 2026-10-05 is File 26-11633.

filed_because: The W013585 production shows Axon proposing, seven weeks before the Council's 2026-10-05 vote on the Outpost amendment, to present its technology to Council members in person in groups of up to two, and shows Department command staff asking the City Manager's office for dates. It contains no record of whether those sessions were scheduled or held, who attended, or what Axon showed them. The Council's approval was conditioned on a community meeting, and no Axon presentation has been given in public. This request asks the City, through the City Clerk as custodian of Council records, for the scheduling, calendar, attendance and material records that would show what happened, and for pre-hearing communications between staff and Council members about the proposal.
notes:
Filed 2026-10-31 at 3:41 PM; auto-acknowledged one second later and forwarded to department(s) for processing. Statutory determination due 2026-11-10. Addressed to the City Clerk (department selector) rather than the Police Department, because the named mailboxes include each Council member and the City Manager's Office. Third request filed 2026-10-31, after W013773 and W013774, so that the two narrower requests carry their own clocks.

2026-11-10 response at 6:18 PM (Martin McTaggart, City Clerk), on the statutory date: "Due to the number of records which are associated with this request, the City will send you records on a rolling production basis"; an initial batch was released; next update no later than 2026-11-17. No Gov. Code § 7922.535(b) citation, no per-item statement, and nothing on whether personal accounts, devices or text messages were searched.

Initial batch: 33 files in native format (29 .eml emails, two .ics calendar files, one PDF and one zip). Every sender and recipient is on a cityofsanmateo.org or axon.com address.
- "Axon briefing for council" (Lt. Riccardi, 2026-08-19) and nine replies through 08-20 among Riccardi, Chief Barberini and McTaggart, with City Manager Khojikian and Laurie Strange addressed. Riccardi, 8/20: "The context for this meeting is to allow the council members direct access to Axon's experts when it comes to the ALPR technology ... We are currently working on starting a trail [sic] with Axon ALPR's and we want the council to be as informed as possible. This should be framed as an executive Q&A for council. This is time sensitive". Later that day: Axon "can do three or four 1 hour sessions with up to two council members at a time."
- The attachment, San_Mateo_PD_Axon_council_session.pdf (2 pages; PDF created 2026-08-19 at 8:27 AM PDT, about ten minutes before Riccardi sent it), is an Axon "Council Demo Day" plan headed "City of San Mateo" and "Prepared by Axon Government Affairs & Account Team · July 2026". Its body still describes Richmond: "Under California's Brown Act, a 'meeting' is triggered when a quorum — a majority — of the body gathers to discuss city business. Richmond's seven-member Council (Mayor + six Councilmembers) has a quorum of four, so keeping each session at two to three members stays safely below that threshold." It lists three identical Council sessions plus a command-staff session, and the topics Outpost, Dedrone, Data Security & Privacy, Ethics Committee & Oversight and Contract Scope & Financials.
- "Council Poll: Axon Technology Briefing Availability" (McTaggart to the Council by Bcc, 2026-08-20) and 16 replies and forwards through 08-28. The file names are numbered 01 to 24; 03, 04, 15, 16, 17, 22 and 23 are not in this batch. The poll offers "several identical one-hour small-group sessions (maximum of two Council Members per session)" on 8/25 and 9/1 and says "The purpose of this briefing is informational only." Replies come from Mayor Loraine and Council Members Diaz Nash, Fernandez and Cwirko-Godycki.
- Scheduling, as far as this batch shows it. 8/24: McTaggart reports "both Lisa and Adam can do tomorrow at 1pm"; Riccardi answers that "we have 2 council members confirmed for tomorrow" and picks the Police Department: "We have the investigations conf room open. Then we have access to our systems if council wanted to see anything." 8/25: Riccardi thanks McTaggart "for helping us get through one of the meetings today" and says Axon will be back on 9/1 "for two 1 hour blocks", with "mayor Loraine and council member Fernandez from 4pm to 5pm" and "the two remaining council members" still to be placed. 8/26: McTaggart relays that Cwirko-Godycki "has requested a 5 p.m. to 6 p.m. slot". The two .ics invitations, both "Axon Briefing with PD" in the Chief's Conference Room on 2026-09-01, list Fernandez and Loraine for 4 to 5 p.m. and Cwirko-Godycki and Newsom for 5 to 6 p.m. All five Council members appear in the scheduling. The batch has no attendance record for either day, so it does not show who attended on 8/25.
- Two messages forwarded by Juliana Santiago (Office of the Chief) to McTaggart on 2026-11-10. In "Meeting with Chief Barberini" (2026-09-23 and 09-24) Axon's Tierney Stuhr writes: "I spoke with Lt Riccardi today regarding the upcoming council meeting on 10/5. Can we please schedule some time with Chief Barberini to prepare?" She later sends "these materials for Chief Barberini to start looking through as a guide for some FAQs" (ALPRCouncilToolkit zip, six Axon PDFs). The other is the accepted invitation to an "Axon Prep Meeting" on 2026-09-29, 4 to 5 p.m., at the Police Department with a Teams link; guests are Santiago, Stuhr, Riccardi, Barberini and Axon's Patrick Newton.
Not in this batch: text messages; any record from a personal account or device; any message sent by the City Manager's office; sign-in or visitor records; whatever Axon showed or left at the Council sessions (item 3); and, for item 4, any exchange between command staff and a Council member other than the scheduling replies.
